1529406.title: AD/.LDAP Test connection is successful using TLS port 636
1529406.initial: Configure LDAP using TLS, with and without certificate  1.Without Certificate: Put LDAP Server behind X0 of sonicwall firewall, In firewall Users>Settings screen Select User authentication method to LDAP, Click on LDAP configure button, Enter the IP address/FQDN of the PC connected to X0 (LDAP server), login user name and password of the server. Uncheck the Require valid certificate from server check box. Check the Use TLS (SSL) check box and set port number to 636(Default LDAP over TLS port (636)),  In the Directory tab, specify a primary domain, In the LDAP Users tab, select 'Trusted Users' as a default LDAP user group, Save the configuration  2.With Certificate: Put LDAP Server behind X0 of sonicwall firewall, Windows Certificate Services must be installed on the LDAP server. Download the CA certificate and save locally. Import the CA certificate .cer file on the firewall  In firewall Users>Settings screen Select User authentication method to LDAP, Click on LDAP configure button, Enter the FQDN of the PC connected to X0 (LDAP server), login user name and password. Check the Require valid certificate from server check box. Check the Use TLS (SSL) set port number to 636(Default LDAP over TLS port (636)),  In the Directory tab, specify a primary domain, In the LDAP Users tab, select 'Trusted Users' as a default LDAP user group, Save the configuration
1529406.steps: 1.Configure LDAP using TLS without certificate as mentioned in the initial setup '1.Without Certificate', Go to Test tab and test the connectivity of the LDAP server  2.Configure LDAP using TLS with certificate as mentioned in the initial setup '2.With Certificate', Go to Test tab and test the connectivity of the LDAP server
1529406.result: Test connectivity of the LDAP server should show success message 'Information returned: Successfully bound as domainName\Administrator' for both with or without certificate

1529415.steps: 1.Create 2 Users user1 and user2 in the AD serve, make user1 as member of group1 and user2 as member of group2  1.Import group 'group1' and 'group2' from ldap server or just create the two groups on firewall  2.On access rule add policy from lan to wan allow DNS service for all users  3.Change the default lan to wan allow all service all user to allow all service for group1  4.Set authentication method to only Radius, and configure Radius in the firewall input correct radius server ip and shared secret  5.Select Use LDAP to retrieve user group information in Radius>Radius Users Tab  6.Enable user login for any LAN interface  7.Login from LAN PC with user a1 and try to visit a WAN website  8.Login from LAN PC with user a2 and try to visit a WAN website
